newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African shares hug opening levels at close.
newsitem.headline: South African shares hug opening levels at close.

text.p: South African shares closed a quiet day near opening levels after earlier dipping lower, dealers said.

"It was a pretty lacklustre day. Everything was fairly flat all day. Even New York's open was disappointing. It opened slightly up before falling. I can't think why our market didn't take a lead from the Dow's Friday finish," one dealer said.
Failing to take heart from Wall Street's gains last week, industrials struggled up in the afternoon before retracing gains. A weak rand contributed to the downbeat tone.
Gold shares fell in morning trade as bullion dropped below $380 an ounce but golds recovered as the metal price broke above the key $380 level once again.

Overall lacklustre trade was seen continuing at least until Wednesday when September CPI data comes out. Some dealers said the flat trade could continue until Friday when September M3 money supply is due.
The overall index was up 7.7 points to 7,011.5, industrials gained 4.5 points to 8,262.9 and golds were up 7.8 points to 1,676.2 points.
